NEB Class 12 Result 2083 — Officially Published

The wait is over. The National Examination Board (NEB) officially published the Class 12 (Grade 12) result for 2083 BS this morning, Friday, Ashadh 5, 2083 (June 19, 2026), following a board meeting held at 8:00 AM. NEB spokesperson Jayanti Satyal confirmed that a total of 4,18,170 students appeared for the examinations, which were held from 14 Baisakh 2083 across the country.

The board reported an overall pass percentage of 64.13%. Within this, the regular category recorded a pass rate of 69.75%, while the partial category recorded 42.38%. The results of 40 students were canceled due to conduct that violated examination ethics and regulations. This year's result was published just 45 days after the exams concluded — notably faster than the roughly three-month wait students faced for the 2082 result last year.

⚡
NEB delivered on its faster turnaround promise Following the same accelerated approach used for the SEE 2082 results, NEB successfully published the Class 12 result within its 45-day target — a significant improvement from the 2–3 month wait of previous years. This is a positive shift for students and families who no longer face the long uncertainty of past result cycles.

Of the total examinees, 2,68,190 students — including 2,31,770 regular and 36,420 partial candidates — received grades in all subjects. The remaining students received an NG (Not Graded) in at least one subject and will have the opportunity to clear it through the upcoming Grade Increment Examination.

How to Check Your NEB Class 12 Result 2083

With the result now live, official websites are experiencing very heavy traffic and may load slowly or time out. If the website is slow, do not panic — try again after a few minutes, or use one of the alternative methods below:

  1. Check online via the official NEB portals Visit neb.gov.np/result or neb.ntc.net.np and enter your symbol number and date of birth to view and download your full marksheet.
  2. Check via SMS Type NEB followed by a space and your symbol number (e.g. NEB 12345678) and send it to 1600 via Nepal Telecom. You will receive your GPA and result details in a reply SMS.
  3. Check via IVR (phone call) Dial 1601 from any phone. Follow the recorded voice instructions, enter your 8-digit symbol number when prompted, and the system will read out your result and GPA.
  4. Check via USSD code Dial *1600# on your NTC network and follow the on-screen prompts to retrieve your result directly on your phone.
📌
Only trust official sources With the result now live, unofficial websites and social media posts may circulate incorrect or outdated information. Always rely on the official NEB portals (neb.gov.np, neb.ntc.net.np) or the SMS/IVR/USSD services above to confirm your actual result.
📝
Found an error in your marksheet? Apply for retotaling now If you believe there is an error in your published result, you can apply for retotaling through the Online Payment (Retotaling) service on neb.gov.np. Applications are open from 11:00 AM on Ashadh 6, 2083 to 5:00 PM on Ashadh 12, 2083 — exactly 7 days from the result publication date. Submit your application within this window, as late requests will not be processed.

Understanding Your Marksheet — The NEB Grading System

Now that your marksheet is available, you will notice NEB does not show a total percentage. Instead, each subject receives a letter grade, and your final result is shown as a GPA (Grade Point Average) — calculated by averaging the grade points of all your subjects. The highest possible GPA is 4.0.

You need a minimum of 35 marks in a subject's theory component to avoid receiving "Not Graded" (NG). If you receive an NG in one or more subjects, this does not mean the end of your academic year — NEB conducts a Grade Increment Examination a few months later, giving you a second opportunity to clear the subject.

📅
Grade Increment Exam timeline for 2083 Based on NEB's academic calendar, the Grade Increment Exam for students with NG is expected from around Bhadra 20, 2083 (early September 2026), with results following a few weeks later — likely around Kartik 2083 (November 2026). Keep an eye on official NEB notices for the confirmed schedule.

You Have Your Result — What Comes Next?

With your result now published, Class 12 is one step in a much longer journey — not the end of it. Whether you scored an A+ or received an NG in one subject, there are strong, well-planned paths forward. Here is how students typically move ahead after their Class 12 result:

Option 01
Bachelor's Degree in Nepal
Apply directly for undergraduate programs at Nepali universities and colleges. A strong, affordable starting point for many fields including medicine, engineering, and management.
Option 02
Study Abroad — Undergraduate
Apply for a Bachelor's program in India, the UK, Australia, the USA, or New Zealand. Your Class 12 result and your IELTS/PTE score are the two key requirements most universities will ask for.
Option 03
Test Preparation First
If you have not yet taken IELTS, PTE, or SAT, this is the ideal window to prepare intensively before university application deadlines for your target intake.
Option 04
Grade Increment (If NG)
If you received an NG in one or two subjects, register for the Grade Increment Exam. This does not delay your overall plans significantly if managed alongside other preparation.

For students considering studying abroad, your Class 12 GPA plays a direct role in which universities and which scholarships you qualify for. Many international universities — particularly in the UK, Australia, and New Zealand — convert your NEB GPA into their own grading equivalent during the admissions assessment. A higher GPA generally opens access to more competitive universities and stronger scholarship opportunities.

🎓
Your result does not have to limit your options Even students with a moderate GPA have strong study abroad pathways available — particularly through foundation programs, diploma-to-degree pathways, and universities that place greater weight on personal statements and English test scores. The right guidance makes a significant difference in identifying which options are genuinely available to you.

Frequently Asked Questions

When was the NEB Class 12 Result 2083 published?
The National Examination Board officially published the Class 12 result on Friday, Ashadh 5, 2083 (June 19, 2026), following a board meeting held at 8:00 AM. This was 45 days after the examinations concluded — significantly faster than the roughly three-month wait for the 2082 result, following the same accelerated approach NEB used for the SEE 2082 results earlier this year.
What was the overall pass percentage for NEB Class 12 Result 2083?
The overall pass percentage was 64.13%. Within this, the regular category recorded a pass rate of 69.75%, while the partial category recorded 42.38%. A total of 4,18,170 students appeared for the examination, of which 2,68,190 students received grades in all subjects. The results of 40 students were canceled due to violations of examination ethics and regulations.
How can I check my NEB Class 12 result online?
Visit neb.gov.np/result or neb.ntc.net.np and enter your symbol number and date of birth to view and download your marksheet. You can also check via SMS by texting NEB followed by a space and your symbol number to 1600, via IVR by dialling 1601, or via USSD by dialling *1600# on your NTC network.
What happens if I get an NG (Not Graded) in a subject?
Receiving an NG means you scored below 35 marks in that subject's theory component. This is not the end of your academic year — NEB conducts a Grade Increment Examination a few months after the main result, giving you the opportunity to clear the subject. Based on the academic calendar, the Grade Increment Exam for 2083 is expected from around Bhadra 2083 (September 2026), with results following in Kartik 2083 (November 2026).
Can I apply for retotaling if I think there is an error in my marksheet?
Yes. NEB's Online Payment (Retotaling) service is open on neb.gov.np from 11:00 AM on Ashadh 6, 2083 to 5:00 PM on Ashadh 12, 2083 — exactly 7 days from the result publication date. If you believe there is an error in your published marks, submit your retotaling application within this window. Applications submitted after the deadline will not be processed, so act quickly if you intend to apply.
Can I apply to study abroad with my NEB Class 12 GPA?
Yes — your NEB Class 12 GPA is a key academic document for undergraduate study abroad applications in the UK, Australia, USA, New Zealand, and India. Most universities convert your GPA into their own grading equivalent during admissions assessment. Combined with an English test score (IELTS, PTE, or equivalent), your Class 12 result determines which universities and scholarships you are eligible for. Even students with a moderate GPA have genuine pathways available through foundation programs and diploma routes.
